newsitem.title: UK: Euro gas oil cargoes stabilise, barges still weak.
newsitem.headline: Euro gas oil cargoes stabilise, barges still weak.

text.p: European gas oil cargo markets showed signs of bottoming out after a heavy fall as the arbitrage from the United States to Europe closed and European traders began to export product to India.
Turkish and Greek demand also supported the market.

Heating oil barges were still under pressure from a lack of demand and premiums fell another dollar on Wednesday to trade at Nov IPE -$1.00/2.00 fob ARA. Nov IPE jumped $2.75 to $211.25 per tonne by 1345 GMT.

Diesel cargo markets, still suffering from the tail-end of an arbitrage from the United States to Europe, were stabilising around Dec IPE +$15/16 cif NWE and a trader said the recent $15 fall in premiums had closed this arbitrage.
Also, U.S. prices were expected to rally following last night's API data showing a small fall in distillate stocks, against expectations of a 2.5 million barrel build.

Heating oil cargoes showed signs of recovery as an arbitrage to India opened from northern Europe and the Med. Russian cargoes loading in Ventspils were in strong demand with offers at the "mean of mean" formula -$4.50 fob versus a -$5.50 bid.
